capmun-2027.about:
CAPMUN (in French, SCONU) is an annual bilingual English–French high-school Model UN held in Canada's National Capital Region.

The conference runs 5–7 March 2027 at Canada's National Capital Region, Ottawa, Canada. It is open to high school students. Working language: English and French (bilingual).

Register through the official site (see FAQ for delegation rules). The delegate fee is published on the official registration page. As at any MUN, delegates research their assigned country, write position papers, give speeches, negotiate in caucuses and draft resolutions — hands-on training in public speaking, research and diplomacy that universities value.
highlights: 5–7 March 2027 in Ottawa, Canada
Bilingual English/French committees
The delegate fee is published on the official registration page
capmun-2027.eligibility: Open to high school students. Working language: English and French (bilingual). No nationality restrictions are stated; international delegates (including from Georgia and Qatar) can apply, arranging their own visa and travel.
how_to_apply: Open the official website (link below) and read the conference information and committee list.
Register through the official site (see FAQ for delegation rules).
Pay the delegate fee by the stated deadline to confirm your place.
Prepare a position paper using the committee study guides before the conference.
capmun-2027.costs: The delegate fee is published on the official registration page. Travel, accommodation and visas are paid by participants unless stated otherwise.

castor-informatique-2026.about:
Castor Informatique is a 45-minute online contest of interactive puzzles about algorithms, logic and data, requiring no prior programming knowledge. Teachers register as coordinators and run the contest with their classes at any time during the window; results and certificates follow.

The contest is in French; students can continue learning programming on France-ioi.org.
highlights: Free, ~700,000 participants
No programming knowledge needed
Run in class, any day in the window
castor-informatique-2026.eligibility: Pupils from CM1 (age ~9) to terminale in French schools, including French schools abroad; entered by a teacher-coordinator.
how_to_apply: Teacher registers as coordinator on castor-informatique.fr
Pick a session date between 8 Nov and 19 Dec 2026
Take the 45-minute contest online in class

cbsmun-2027.about:
CBSMUN is the Nordic university MUN hosted by Copenhagen Business School, with a focus on economics and sustainability. Expect 4 days, about 10 committees, 3 socials and 200+ delegates.

The conference runs 11–14 March 2027 at Copenhagen Business School, Frederiksberg, Denmark. It is open to university students from any country. Working language: English.

The organisers have announced the dates ('save the date'); delegate applications open on the official site — check the FAQ for delegation and payment details. The delegate fee is published on the official registration page. As at any MUN, delegates research their assigned country, write position papers, give speeches, negotiate in caucuses and draft resolutions — hands-on training in public speaking, research and diplomacy that universities value.
highlights: 11–14 March 2027 in Copenhagen, Denmark
Nordic university MUN with an economics and sustainability focus
The delegate fee is published on the official registration page
cbsmun-2027.eligibility: Open to university students from any country. Working language: English. No nationality restrictions are stated; international delegates (including from Georgia and Qatar) can apply, arranging their own visa and travel.
how_to_apply: Open the official website (link below) and read the conference information and committee list.
The organisers have announced the dates ('save the date'); delegate applications open on the official site — check the FAQ for delegation and payment details.
Pay the delegate fee by the stated deadline to confirm your place.
Prepare a position paper using the committee study guides before the conference.
cbsmun-2027.costs: The delegate fee is published on the official registration page. Travel, accommodation and visas are paid by participants unless stated otherwise.

cee-national-economics-challenge-2027.about:
The National Economics Challenge (NEC) has two divisions: the Adam Smith division for AP/IB/honours students and the David Ricardo division for general economics students. Teams of 3–4 compete in online qualifying rounds and state competitions, with top teams advancing to the national semifinals and finals.

It is the leading US high-school economics team competition and a strong signal for economics and business applicants.
highlights: Two divisions by course level
Team-based, online qualifiers
National finals for top teams
cee-national-economics-challenge-2027.eligibility: Teams of US high-school students with a teacher advisor.
how_to_apply: Sign up for updates on the CEE page
Form a team with your economics teacher
Register when your state opens (Nov 2026–Jan 2027)
Compete in the online/state rounds from January 2027

ceepus-mobility-2027-28.about:
CEEPUS is an intergovernmental university exchange programme between Albania, Austria, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Bulgaria, Croatia, Czech Republic, Hungary, Kosovo, Moldova, Montenegro, North Macedonia, Poland, Romania, Serbia, Slovakia and Slovenia. Host countries pay a monthly grant (accommodation and living support) to incoming students and teachers.

Students who have fully completed two semesters at a CEEPUS university can go on network mobility (if their department belongs to a CEEPUS network) or as a 'freemover' (limited grants, in some countries only for the summer term). Citizenship of a member state is generally required. University networks apply for the 2027-28 year by 30 November 2026; students then apply online through ceepus.info for the mobility offered by their network or their National CEEPUS Office.
highlights: 16 member countries incl. Moldova, Serbia, Romania, Poland
Host-country grant covers living costs
Network or freemover routes
ceepus-mobility-2027-28.eligibility: Students enrolled at a university in a CEEPUS member country who have completed two semesters (one for intensive courses); generally citizens of a member state. Studying in your own country is not allowed.
how_to_apply: Ask your international office whether your department is in a CEEPUS network
Register on ceepus.info
Apply online for network or freemover mobility by the deadline set for your term
Get the host university's acceptance letter
ceepus-mobility-2027-28.costs: Host-country monthly grant; travel normally not covered.

cern-summer-student-programme-2027.about:
The CERN Summer Student Programme brings several hundred students to the world's largest particle physics laboratory near Geneva each summer. Each student joins an experimental, theoretical, computing or engineering team for 8–13 weeks, works on a real project, and follows a dedicated lecture series given by CERN scientists, plus visits to experiments and a student poster session.

CERN says all nationalities are welcome to apply (students from Canada, Japan and the US apply through their national schemes). Successful candidates receive a net subsistence allowance of CHF 94 per calendar day, and travel to and from Geneva may be covered. It is one of the most prestigious summer experiences for anyone considering a career in physics or scientific computing.
highlights: Work on a real project in a CERN team for 2–3 months
Dedicated summer lecture programme on particle physics and computing
Daily allowance of CHF 94 (net); travel may be covered
cern-summer-student-programme-2027.eligibility: Bachelor's or master's students (not PhD) in physics, engineering, computer science or mathematics with at least 6 semesters of full-time study completed by the start, still enrolled full-time, with good English. Must not have attended before or worked at CERN for more than 3 months. All nationalities welcome; Canadian, Japanese and US students use their national schemes.
how_to_apply: Check careers.cern/summer from late 2026 for the 2027 Summer Student vacancy
Prepare a CV, motivation letter and transcripts
Arrange two reference letters (referees submit online)
Submit before the end of January 2027
Selection results are usually communicated in spring
cern-summer-student-programme-2027.costs: Net subsistence allowance of CHF 94 per calendar day (health insurance deducted). Travel to/from Geneva may be covered depending on circumstances. No fee to apply.

ceu-summer-university-2027.about:
CEU Summer University (SUN) has run for 30 years and offers one- and two-week advanced courses taught by international faculty on topics such as democracy and citizenship, human rights, Roma studies, higher-education policy, history and philosophy. Participants come from dozens of countries, many from Central and Eastern Europe, the Caucasus and Central Asia.

Tuition in 2026 was around EUR 500–650 per course, but SUN is not-for-profit and offers a flexible, need-based system of partial and full tuition waivers plus scholarships towards travel and accommodation; these must be requested at the application stage with strong justification.
highlights: Advanced courses with international faculty and a very diverse cohort
Full and partial tuition waivers plus travel/accommodation grants
Strong fit for students from the Caucasus and Central/Eastern Europe
ceu-summer-university-2027.eligibility: Mainly master's and PhD students, junior faculty and professionals in relevant fields; some courses accept advanced undergraduates. Check each course's eligibility. Good English required. Open to all nationalities.
how_to_apply: Browse the 2027 courses (published around early December 2026)
Pick a course and check its specific requirements
Apply online with CV, motivation and any course-specific documents
Request a tuition waiver/scholarship in the application if needed (deadline 1 March in 2026)
Self-funded applicants without visa needs had until 15 April in 2026
ceu-summer-university-2027.costs: Tuition roughly EUR 500–650 per course (2026). Need-based full/partial tuition waivers and scholarships for travel and accommodation available.

cfa-institute-research-challenge-2026-27.about:
The Research Challenge gives students hands-on mentoring and training in financial analysis. Each team, guided by a faculty advisor and an industry mentor, researches an assigned company, meets its management, writes a professional equity research report and presents to a panel of investment professionals.

Winners progress from local to sub-regional, regional and global rounds (Americas, EMEA and Asia Pacific). It is one of the best-known finance competitions for students targeting investment careers.
highlights: Real company analysis with industry mentors
Local to global rounds
Global Final in Singapore, May 2027
cfa-institute-research-challenge-2026-27.eligibility: Teams of 3–5 undergraduate or graduate students from a university participating through its local CFA society.
how_to_apply: Check whether your university participates (CFA Institute site)
Form a team with a faculty advisor
Register with your local CFA society
Research the assigned company and submit the report
cfa-institute-research-challenge-2026-27.costs: Free for students; travel to later rounds is often funded by organisers/sponsors.

ciee-summer-abroad-high-school-2027.about:
CIEE's high-school Summer Abroad programmes send U.S. high-school students for 3, 4 or 8 weeks of language immersion, arts, STEM or service-learning in about 30 destinations, including Argentina, Botswana, Ghana, Japan, Morocco, South Korea, Spain and Taiwan. Language & Culture programmes (4 weeks) can earn 4 college credits; tuition includes medical and travel protection.

CIEE says about US$10 million in scholarships is available each year (including need-based Global Navigator awards). CIEE also runs semester/year High School Abroad, gap-year and first-year-of-college abroad programmes. Apply via my.ciee.org; contact hsabroad@ciee.org for 2027 prices and scholarship deadlines.
highlights: ~30 summer destinations
College credit for language programmes
US$10M scholarships yearly
how_to_apply: Pick a summer programme on ciee.org
Apply on my.ciee.org
Apply for CIEE scholarships (e.g., Global Navigator)
Pre-departure orientation
ciee-summer-abroad-high-school-2027.costs: Programme tuition per destination; about US$10 million in scholarships each year.

cje-locked-out-youth-exchange-peniche-20.about:
Locked Out is an Erasmus+ youth exchange run by Clube de Jovens Europeus (CJE) in Peniche, Portugal, with around 40 young people from Portugal, Spain, Czechia, Hungary and Slovakia (mobility 25 November – 1 December 2026; travel days 24 November and 2 December). It explores the barriers young people face (no experience, no money, language, gender, background, where you live) and how to get past them.

In international teams, participants pick a real barrier and build an escape room where every puzzle represents part of it, ending with a 'key': a real programme, right, support network or skill. Teams then swap rooms. The programme includes an online preparatory meeting, team-building, an intercultural night, and a follow-up dissemination activity at home. Participants stay at Peniche Surf Camp near Baleal beach and receive a Youthpass.

No experience is needed: puzzles need logic, creativity, building and storytelling, whatever your level of English.
highlights: Creative, hands-on format: design and build escape rooms
Group travel tickets from national meeting points bought by the organiser
Surf town venue on the Atlantic, Youthpass certificate
cje-locked-out-youth-exchange-peniche-20.eligibility: Residents or citizens of Portugal, Spain, Czechia, Hungary or Slovakia, ideally aged 18–25, available for the whole mobility and willing to run a dissemination activity afterwards. Applicants must not currently receive other EU funds (e.g. an Erasmus university grant). No prior experience required.
how_to_apply: Read the full call on the CJE website.
Apply through the E29 participant portal linked on the page by 1 November 2026 (applications are reviewed daily).
Watch for the selection email (2–10 November 2026) and confirm within 24 hours.
Pay the EUR 50 refundable deposit and join the group's Discord channel for travel details.
cje-locked-out-youth-exchange-peniche-20.costs: Travel (from national meeting points), accommodation in shared rooms and three meals a day are co-funded by Erasmus+. Selected participants pay a EUR 50 deposit, refunded after the mobility. Participants bring a European Health Insurance Card; surf lessons are optional at own cost.

climatelaunchpad-2027.about:
ClimateLaunchpad is EIT Climate-KIC's global competition for early-stage green business ideas, running in dozens of countries each year. Teams with an idea or early innovation that cuts emissions or helps adaptation join a bootcamp, receive coaching and pitch first at a national final.

National winners progress to regional and global finals, gaining visibility with investors, corporates and the Climate-KIC network; successful teams can continue into incubation programmes. Many participants are students and recent graduates.

In 2026 applications were open March–May; the 2027 edition is expected to follow the same pattern. Check the site for the list of participating countries.
highlights: Free bootcamp and coaching for climate start-up ideas
National, regional and global pitch finals
Route into Climate-KIC incubation
climatelaunchpad-2027.eligibility: Teams (or individuals) with an early-stage green business idea in a participating country; check the site for the 2027 country list.
how_to_apply: Check whether your country takes part in the 2027 edition.
Prepare a short description of your climate solution and team.
Apply online when applications open (expected March 2027).
Attend the national bootcamp and pitch at the national final.

cmunc-xxv-2027.about:
CMUNC is Cornell University's high-school Model UN, run by the Cornell International Affairs Society, now in its 25th session.

The conference runs 22–25 April 2027 at Cornell University, Ithaca, United States. It is open to high school students and school delegations. Working language: English.

Registration for CMUNC XXV is now open on the official site. The delegate fee is published on the official registration page. As at any MUN, delegates research their assigned country, write position papers, give speeches, negotiate in caucuses and draft resolutions — hands-on training in public speaking, research and diplomacy that universities value.
highlights: 22–25 April 2027 in Ithaca, United States
Ivy League campus experience
The delegate fee is published on the official registration page
cmunc-xxv-2027.eligibility: Open to high school students and school delegations. Working language: English. No nationality restrictions are stated; international delegates (including from Georgia and Qatar) can apply, arranging their own visa and travel.
how_to_apply: Open the official website (link below) and read the conference information and committee list.
Registration for CMUNC XXV is now open on the official site.
Pay the delegate fee by the stated deadline to confirm your place.
Prepare a position paper using the committee study guides before the conference.
cmunc-xxv-2027.costs: The delegate fee is published on the official registration page. Travel, accommodation and visas are paid by participants unless stated otherwise.

coci-2026-27.about:
COCI is a long-running monthly-style contest series used by olympiad students around the world to train for national olympiads and the IOI. Each round is a three-hour online contest with several algorithmic problems in increasing difficulty, solved in C++, Python or other supported languages and judged automatically.

All rounds start at 14:00 UTC. Rankings are published per round and for the season; problems and test data are released afterwards for practice.
highlights: Free, online, open worldwide
IOI-style algorithmic problems
Season ranking across five rounds
coci-2026-27.eligibility: Open to anyone; aimed at secondary-school students preparing for informatics olympiads.
how_to_apply: Create an account on the COCI/HSIN evaluator
Join each round at 14:00 UTC on the contest date
Solve as many problems as you can in three hours
Check results and upsolve with the published test data

codam-amsterdam-tuition-free-coding-scho.about:
Codam (42 Amsterdam) is the Amsterdam campus of 42, the network of tuition-free computer-science schools founded in Paris in 2013 with more than 50 campuses in over 30 countries. There are no teachers, lectures or fees: students learn by building projects and reviewing each other's code, and the campus is usually open 24/7.

Anyone aged 18 or over can apply, with no diploma or previous coding experience required. You register online, take a short logic/aptitude test, attend an introduction session and then a full-time, on-site four-week 'Piscine' (selection bootcamp in C and shell). Piscine sessions are scheduled several times a year; the campus site lists upcoming dates after you register. Those who succeed join the core curriculum (about 12-18 months) and can then specialise (AI, cybersecurity, graphics, etc.), with internships along the way.

Teaching is in English. Tuition is free; students cover their own housing and living costs and, for non-residents, visa requirements.
highlights: 100% tuition-free, peer-to-peer, project-based learning
No diploma or coding experience needed; 18+
Part of the global 42 Network (50+ campuses)
codam-amsterdam-tuition-free-coding-scho.eligibility: Anyone aged 18 or over, any nationality, no diploma or prior coding required. Non-residents need the right to stay in Netherlands for the Piscine and studies. Working language: English.
how_to_apply: Create an account on the campus website and take the online logic test.
Book an introduction/check-in meeting.
Choose and attend a four-week on-site Piscine.
If selected, start the core curriculum.
codam-amsterdam-tuition-free-coding-scho.costs: Tuition-free. Housing, food, travel and visa costs are the student's own.

code-first-girls-cfgdegree.about:
Code First Girls is a UK-based social enterprise that has taught coding to a large community of women across 100+ countries. Its free offers include the Coding Kickstarter (self-paced introductory courses) and the CFGdegree, an intensive 16-week online programme in software engineering, data or product, plus a 4-week +Masters top-up.

Courses are funded by partner companies, who also recruit from graduates. There is a Mid-Level Accelerator for women with at least 1.5 years in tech.

Applications are made online for each intake; seats are limited and some courses prioritise UK residents, so check the eligibility of each intake.
highlights: Free intensive 16-week CFGdegree
Software, data and product tracks
Hiring links with partner companies
code-first-girls-cfgdegree.eligibility: Women and non-binary people aged 18+; some intakes are limited to UK residents or specific profiles.
how_to_apply: Create an account on the Code First Girls website.
Choose Kickstarter or CFGdegree and check the intake's eligibility.
Complete the application/assessment.
Join the cohort when it starts.

codeyourfuture-free-software-training.about:
CodeYourFuture is a UK charity that trains people from low-income and refugee backgrounds to become software developers. Volunteers from the tech industry teach the course, which runs from a short Intro to Digital (20-40 hours) to the 13-week Intro to Programming and on to a full software development course, about five months in total to an entry-level role.

Classes meet in Birmingham, Glasgow, London, Manchester, Sheffield and Cape Town. Eligibility: over 18, low income (below 60% of regional median after housing and taxes), living within 90 minutes by public transport of a hub, and passing a free English test.

There is no fee; travel, lunch and childcare are covered on class days. Sign-up is online and rolling.
highlights: Free, with travel, lunch and childcare covered
Taught by volunteers from tech companies
Strong support for refugees and career-changers
codeyourfuture-free-software-training.eligibility: Adults 18+ on low income living within 90 minutes of a hub (UK cities or Cape Town); free English test required.
how_to_apply: Sign up at course1.codeyourfuture.io.
Complete Intro to Digital.
Pass the English test and join Intro to Programming.
Progress to the full software development course.
codeyourfuture-free-software-training.costs: Free; travel, lunch and childcare costs on class days are covered.

college-of-europe-eu-diplomatic-programm.about:
The European Union Diplomatic Programme for the Enlargement Region (EUDP) is a five-month residential programme run by the College of Europe and funded by the European Commission's Directorate-General for Enlargement and Eastern Neighbourhood (DG ENEST). Its fifth edition is expected to run from 1 February to 2 July 2027.

The aim is to build regional cooperation and an "esprit de corps" between diplomats and officials from the enlargement region and their EU peers, while deepening their knowledge of EU affairs. The curriculum includes joint activities with the European Union Diplomatic Academy (funded by the EEAS).

The call targets diplomats and officials working on foreign policy and EU accession from Georgia (subject to the evolution of the political situation), Moldova, Ukraine, the Western Balkans and Türkiye. Candidates need completed university studies, professional experience in or knowledge of EU affairs and accession, and fluent English; French is an asset.
highlights: Five months at the College of Europe with EU-funded places
Joint sessions with the EU Diplomatic Academy
Network with diplomats from across the enlargement region
college-of-europe-eu-diplomatic-programm.eligibility: Diplomats and/or officials working on foreign policy and EU accession from Georgia (subject to political developments), Moldova, Ukraine, the Western Balkans or Türkiye; completed university degree; experience in or knowledge of EU affairs/accession; fluent written and spoken English (French an asset).
how_to_apply: Read the College of Europe EUDP call (linked from the EU NEIGHBOURS east page)
Check with your ministry/institution about nomination or support
Submit the application by 15 November 2026
college-of-europe-eu-diplomatic-programm.costs: Funded by the European Commission (DG ENEST); see the call for details of what is covered.

columbia-pre-college-summer-2027.about:
Columbia Pre-College offers intensive, university-style courses for high-school students in subjects from business, law and international relations to computer science, engineering, creative writing and pre-med. Students choose NYC Residential (three weeks, living in Columbia housing), NYC Commuter (one or three weeks) or Online (one or two weeks), and receive a certificate and written evaluation.

2027 sessions: Residential A 28 June – 16 July and B 20 July – 6 August; commuter and online sessions run from 21 June to 6 August, and the credit-bearing College Edge runs 24 May – 13 August. International students attend every year; residential students need a visa if not American.
highlights: Courses taught on Columbia's Morningside Heights campus in New York
Residential, commuter or online formats
Early-deadline option on 1 February 2027
columbia-pre-college-summer-2027.eligibility: High-school students (typically grades 9–12) from any country with sufficient English proficiency; check the programme policies for age and English requirements.
how_to_apply: Browse 2027 summer courses on the Columbia Pre-College site
Start the online application when it opens in mid-November 2026
Submit transcript, statement and any English test required for international students
Apply by 1 February 2027 (early) or 1 March 2027 (residential general deadline)
columbia-pre-college-summer-2027.costs: Paid programme; tuition, housing and fees are listed on the programme-costs page. Limited financial aid may be available; check the site.

comun-2027.about:
COMUN is the Model UN of the Coornhert Gymnasium in Gouda. The 2027 theme is 'Empowering public voices: strengthening civil society', and the site has a dedicated first-timer page plus social activities that show off the city.

The conference runs 12–14 February 2027 at the Coornhert Gymnasium, Gouda, Netherlands. It is open to secondary school students in school delegations; first-timers welcome. Working language: English.

Schools register following the instructions in the official mailings on the site. The delegate fee is published on the official registration page. Details are in the conference mailings. As at any MUN, delegates research their assigned country, write position papers, give speeches, negotiate in caucuses and draft resolutions — hands-on training in public speaking, research and diplomacy that universities value.
highlights: 12–14 February 2027 in Gouda, Netherlands
First-timer support page
The delegate fee is published on the official registration page
comun-2027.eligibility: Open to secondary school students in school delegations; first-timers welcome. Working language: English. No nationality restrictions are stated; international delegates (including from Georgia and Qatar) can apply, arranging their own visa and travel.
how_to_apply: Open the official website (link below) and read the conference information and committee list.
Schools register following the instructions in the official mailings on the site.
Pay the delegate fee by the stated deadline to confirm your place.
Prepare a position paper using the committee study guides before the conference.
comun-2027.costs: The delegate fee is published on the official registration page. Details are in the conference mailings. Travel, accommodation and visas are paid by participants unless stated otherwise.

conception-x-venture-scientist-spring-20.about:
Conception X is a UK-based programme that trains PhD students and early researchers to become 'venture scientists' and build startups from their research. The Spring 2027 cohort (Venture Scientist 100) takes about 100 researchers from leading European institutions.

Over nine months, run alongside the PhD, participants join 18 co-building sessions, get expert coaching and join a peer community; the strongest teams can receive investment. Past ventures range from robotics and materials to biotech and climate tech.

Applications for the Spring 2027 cohorts close on 6 December 2026; Conception X also runs online discovery sessions for questions.
highlights: Built for technical PhD students, alongside their studies
18 co-building sessions plus coaching
Investment available for top teams
conception-x-venture-scientist-spring-20.eligibility: Technical PhD students (and similar early researchers) at European research institutions with a research-based venture idea. Check the site for the participating universities.
how_to_apply: Read the programme page and attend a discovery session if unsure.
Prepare a short description of your research and its commercial potential.
Submit the online application by 6 December 2026.
Interview if shortlisted.
conception-x-venture-scientist-spring-20.costs: No participation fee stated; investment terms for top teams are set by Conception X.

cranmer-awards-2027.about:
The Cranmer Awards celebrate the language of the Book of Common Prayer through recitation, with Junior (11–14) and Senior (15–18) categories, regional heats across the UK and a national final held on the last Saturday of February. Since 2027 there is also a poetry strand: students write a verse about Thomas Cranmer, and shortlisted poems are displayed and voted on at the national final.

Open to young people of all backgrounds and faiths; a good opportunity for students interested in English literature, drama and public speaking.
highlights: Recitation and poetry strands
Junior and Senior categories
National final in York
cranmer-awards-2027.eligibility: Young people aged 11–18 of any background or faith (UK-based heats).
how_to_apply: Choose recitation or poetry
Apply online on pbs.org.uk
Submit by Sunday 6 Dec 2026
Compete at a regional heat; finalists go to York

creative-hq-fintech-lab-2027.about:
Fintech Lab is Creative HQ's accelerator for early-stage fintech startups, run with partners from New Zealand's financial sector. The 2027 programme is hybrid: teams work mostly remotely and come together in person three times, starting with a kick-off in Wellington on 16-19 March 2027 alongside NZ's Fintech Hui and a midway point in Auckland on 5-6 May.

Startups get structured coaching, access to banks, regulators and investors, and a demo day. Thanks to partners, it is free and no equity is taken.

Applications are open until 22 November 2026 via the 'Apply here' link. It best suits founders who are, or plan to be, building for the New Zealand/Australian market.
highlights: Free and equity-free
Access to NZ banks, regulators and investors
Hybrid with three in-person meetups
creative-hq-fintech-lab-2027.eligibility: Early-stage fintech startups; teams must be able to attend the in-person sessions in New Zealand.
how_to_apply: Read the Fintech Lab page and key dates.
Prepare a short description of your product, team and traction.
Apply online by 22 November 2026.
Interview if shortlisted.
creative-hq-fintech-lab-2027.costs: Free; no equity. Travel to New Zealand sessions is at the startup's own cost.

critical-language-scholarship-2027.about:
The Critical Language Scholarship (CLS) Program is a U.S. government summer programme for American undergraduate and graduate students to study one of nine critical languages: Arabic, Chinese, Hindi, Japanese, Korean, Persian, Portuguese, Russian or Swahili. Institutes are held overseas (intensive classes, cultural activities, often homestays) or virtually for undergraduates.

It is a competitive, merit-based scholarship that covers programme costs for selected participants; some languages require prior study. Applicants must be U.S. citizens or nationals aged 18+ by 15 May 2027, enrolled in a U.S. degree programme and, for undergraduates, have completed one year of study by summer. Apply once per year for one language by 17 November 2026 (8 pm Eastern).
highlights: Nine critical languages, overseas or virtual
Fully funded by the U.S. State Department
Deadline 17 November 2026
critical-language-scholarship-2027.eligibility: U.S. citizens/nationals, 18+ by 15 May 2027, enrolled in an accredited U.S. undergraduate or graduate degree programme (enrolled in fall 2026 and spring 2027 unless graduating in December); undergraduates must finish one full year of study before the programme; meet language prerequisites.
how_to_apply: Check eligibility and language prerequisites on clscholarship.org
Choose one language
Submit the online application with essays and recommendations by 17 Nov 2026, 8 pm ET
Await selection results in spring 2027
critical-language-scholarship-2027.costs: Fully funded for selected participants (programme costs paid by the U.S. Department of State).

cshl-undergraduate-research-program-2027.about:
The URP brings about 25 undergraduates to Cold Spring Harbor Laboratory on Long Island, home of eight Nobel laureates, for a mentored original research project with a CSHL faculty member. Alongside lab work there are seminars, a journal club, career discussions and a final symposium. Students with engineering, chemistry, computer science, maths or physics backgrounds are welcome, not only biologists.

CSHL says students of any nationality are eligible and no TOEFL/IELTS is required, but foreign students normally must be enrolled full-time at a US college or (in limited cases) at a foreign university with a CSHL agreement. Participants receive a USD 7,000 stipend and free housing in campus cabins and meals.
highlights: Original research project with a CSHL faculty mentor
USD 7,000 stipend plus room and board
No English test required

cuhk-international-summer-school-2027.about:
The CUHK International Summer School (ISS) lets students take up to two three-credit courses in five academic areas, taught in English by CUHK and visiting overseas professors, as well as beginner Putonghua or Cantonese. The 2026 July session ran 21 June – 29 July with about 20 content courses, on-campus hostel accommodation, orientation, a farewell dinner and weekend cultural excursions around Hong Kong; an August session is also offered.

It is open to full-time undergraduates and to high-school seniors with a confirmed university offer. Students whose university is a CUHK exchange partner may be nominated (tuition waived); everyone else applies as a non-local fee-paying student.

Chinese language (Putonghua/Cantonese) plus English-taught courses
On-campus hostel and Hong Kong cultural programme

culture-moves-europe-individual-mobility.about:
Culture Moves Europe is the European Union's mobility scheme for the cultural and creative sectors, funded by Creative Europe and implemented by the Goethe-Institut. With €25 million for 2025–2028 it supports around 7,000 artists, cultural professionals and hosts to travel abroad, develop international projects and partnerships, learn, and reach new audiences.

The 2026–2027 individual mobility call is open to artists and cultural professionals aged 18+ who are legal residents of a Creative Europe participating country, which includes Georgia, Armenia, Moldova and Ukraine. Eligible fields are architecture, cultural heritage, design and fashion design, literature, music, performing arts and visual arts. You can apply alone or as a group of up to five, and both emerging and established professionals are welcome.

The grant gives €85 per day of project implementation plus a travel allowance, with top-ups for green travel (€400), visas (€120) and children under 18 (€200 each). Applications are evaluated at the end of every month until 30 April 2027.

Open to residents of Georgia and other Creative Europe countries
Rolling call: decisions every month until April 2027

CUMUN is the flagship conference of the Chittagong University Model United Nations Association (CUMUNA, est. 2014). The 11th edition runs for four days, 20–23 January 2027, on the University of Chittagong campus, under the theme 'Revitalizing Global Governance Through Strategic and Societal Adaptability to Strengthen Multilateralism for a Sustainable Future'.

Nine committees and more than 400 delegates are expected, following 400+ at CUMUN 2026. It welcomes school and university students and executive-board applicants.

A well-established four-day conference and a good option for students in Bangladesh and neighbouring countries.

daad-rise-germany-2027.about:
RISE Germany (Research Internships in Science and Engineering) matches undergraduates with research groups across Germany for a three-month summer internship. Students pick projects from an online database of offers in biology, chemistry, physics, earth sciences and engineering, and work alongside a doctoral student who acts as mentor. The working language is English.

DAAD pays a monthly stipend towards living costs, host institutions help with housing, and interns join a DAAD network meeting. Eligibility depends on where you study, not your passport: international students enrolled at universities in the US, Canada, the UK or Ireland can apply.

No German required

Upload CV, transcript and motivation letters
Ask referees to submit letters by 15 December 2026
Submit by 30 November 2026; hosts rank applicants in January
daad-rise-germany-2027.costs: DAAD monthly stipend for three months (amount set by DAAD) towards living costs; hosts assist with housing. No fee.

daad-university-summer-course-grants-geo.about:
The DAAD University Summer Courses programme funds students and graduates to deepen their German (general and subject-specific language) and their knowledge of Germany through a four-week summer course at a German university or higher-education institution. Courses run between June and September, with at least 25 teaching hours per week, in person only and taught in German.

The grant covers the course fee, accommodation arranged by the course provider (single room in a dorm, shared flat or private household), a one-time allowance of €475, a country-specific travel allowance, and health, accident and liability insurance. It can only be received once.

Students in Georgia apply directly through the DAAD portal: applications open on 1 September and close on 30 October each year. The 2026 round has just closed, so the next opportunity is the autumn 2027 call for summer 2028 courses. Use the year to reach at least A2 German and get a certificate (Goethe, TestDaF, onSET, telc, ÖSD, DSD).
highlights: Course fee, accommodation and €475 allowance covered
Travel allowance and insurance included
Wide choice of university summer courses across Germany
daad-university-summer-course-grants-geo.eligibility: Students and graduates of any subject enrolled at a university in an eligible country such as Georgia (not Germany), aged 18+ at course start; Bachelor's students must have completed at least two years of study; final-year students only if they plan postgraduate study; German at least A2 with a recent certificate.
how_to_apply: Pick a course from the DAAD summer-course list (Excel/PDF on the DAAD page)
Prepare a CV and motivation letter in German, transcripts and a German certificate (min. A2)
Apply in the DAAD portal between 1 September and 30 October 2027
Wait for the selection committee decision (academic record and motivation are key)
daad-university-summer-course-grants-geo.costs: Fully funded: course fees, accommodation, €475 allowance, travel subsidy and insurance.

The programme is international and fully supported: free accommodation in the DESY hostel for the whole stay, a salary of EUR 28.50 per day and at least partial reimbursement of travel costs. The 2027 call is being prepared; watch the website for the opening.

dfjw-brigitte-sauzay-programme.about:
The Brigitte Sauzay Programme is a reciprocal exchange for pupils learning French (in Germany) or German (in France). Each partner spends at least three months with the other's family and attends school there, and the two stays can fall in one or two school years.

You find your partner yourself, for example through DFJW's online classifieds, agree dates with both schools and fill in the exchange dossier. DFJW pays a travel-cost grant if you apply online at least one month before the stay. It is a low-cost way to spend a term abroad without an agency.

DFJW travel grant

dfjw-voltaire-programme-2027-28.about:
The Voltaire Programme is a reciprocal one-to-one exchange run by the Franco-German Youth Office (DFJW/OFAJ). Pupils in grades 8, 9 or 10 who learn French (and French pupils learning German) spend six months living with their partner's family and attending school in France, then host the partner for six months at home. You can apply alone and be matched, or apply with a partner you already know.

It is one of the most immersive ways to become fluent in French or German without paying an agency: the families host each other and DFJW supports the exchange with preparation, support and a grant. Applications for the 2027/2028 campaign close on 6 November 2026; the next campaign opens on 1 August 2027.

Deadline 6 November 2026

Get matched with a partner (or name your own)

doc-new-zealand-conservation-volunteerin.about:
The Department of Conservation (DOC) manages New Zealand's national parks and protected areas and runs a large volunteer programme. On its website you can search volunteer activities by region, type, time commitment and fitness level; some are run by DOC directly and others by community conservation groups linked from the listings.

International visitors can volunteer if they are already in New Zealand and allowed to stay for the length of the activity; no work visa is needed because the roles are unpaid. Some roles need a police certificate (in English), and DOC strongly recommends comprehensive travel insurance.

It is a good option for gap-year students, working-holiday visitors and anyone studying environmental science who wants hands-on fieldwork with an official agency.

doc-new-zealand-conservation-volunteerin.costs: Volunteering is free. Travel to New Zealand, insurance and living costs are yours; some longer DOC roles may provide accommodation (check each listing).

Besides capital, founders join the DRF community of student investors and alumni founders, with access to mentoring and introductions to later-stage investors.
